Ira: Quick heads-up — noticed a race in the metering handshake when two partial attributions arrive for the same request id and both try to stamp owner_account.
Sam: repro steps? where are the two attributions originating from?
Ira: client sends a chunked request -> proxy splits into two downstream calls for embeddings + textgen. each returns attribution asynchronously. sometimes the first one falls into the delayed-retry path and second wins the ownership write.
Mona: so ownership is not idempotent. we only have last-write-wins on the owner field today, right?
Ira: correct. LWW causes two problems: incorrect billed owner and a missed audit trail linking both fragments.
Oliver: can we derive owner from stable provenance (client_id + session_id + request_nonce) instead of write order?
Tara: that would require changing provenance envelope — we would need a canonicalization step at the gateway before we fan out. might be heavy but doable.
Sam: alternatives: 1) make ownership write idempotent with compare-and-swap using an epoch token, 2) buffer at attribution aggregator until both parts resolved, 3) attach fragment pointers and compute final ownership in a later reconciliation.
Mona: preference for option 1 for low-latency: CAS on owner field, write only if owner is empty or matches our token. we already have token metadata on the event header. downside: more conditional writes and some failed CASs we need to surface.
Ira: CAS reduces mis-billing but doesn't capture the second contributor in audit. we still lose contributor metadata unless we append provenance list instead of single owner.
Oliver: append list could bloat storage but keep fixed-size ring of up to 3 contributors. storage tradeoff seems reasonable given most events are single-owner.
Tara: ops question: how do we reconcile billing when CAS fails? do we enqueue to backfill queue?
Sam: propose: on CAS failure, emit an audit-event to audit-log topic with both fragments' metadata and an action pointer. reconciliation job consumes audits and performs final attribution once window elapses.
Ira: that makes sense. keep fast path for CAS success, slow path for audits + backfill. ensures SLAs for common case.
Mona: we should also add a short-lived in-memory dedupe at the aggregator (50ms window) to collapse near-simultaneous attrib writes from split fanouts. cheap and helps a lot.
Oliver: agree. also ensure event ids are normalized: use canonical hex of sha256(request_nonce||client_id) so both fragments produce same id.
Tara: do we need schema changes? audit-event needs contributor array and reason enum {cas_conflict, delayed_retry, partial_failure}.
Sam: minimal schema change: add optional contributors:[], conflict_reason:string. consumers can safely ignore if absent.
Ira: deployment plan? we can implement CAS + canonical ids + short dedupe as v1. Emit audit-events on CAS miss. Later add ring append and offline reconciliation job.
Mona: testing: integration test that simulates 1000 concurrent split requests, verify no unaccounted tokens and audit-events <= 1% of requests.
Oliver: also add metric meters.cas_conflicts and meters.audit_events_emitted, dashboards in console.
Tara: ops: during rollout enable feature flag for a subset of accounts. monitor billing deltas.
Sam: PR checklist: update ingest proto, add CAS helper in attribution store, implement dedupe cache at aggregator, add reconciliation consumer skeleton.
Ira: thanks. I'll open an RFC-lite with the plan and a timeline. assigning follow-ups: Sam -> store CAS helper, Mona -> aggregator dedupe, Oliver -> id canonicalization, Tara -> rollout/monitoring, Ira -> audit consumer skeleton.
deploy-bot: Deployment started for infra/attribution-cas on canary 3.
Sam: ack, I'll watch the metrics. :eyes:
Mona: if anyone sees unexpected spike in audit_events_emitted ping me. :zap:
